packageRules.description: Action bumps are low-risk and arrive in bursts — one round of checkout/setup-java/cache/upload-artifact majors landed as six separate PRs. Batch non-major action updates into a single PR; majors still get their own so the breaking-change notes actually get read. Kept first in the list so the more specific rules below can override the group for actions that have to ship alongside their library half.

compose-ai-tools ships the preview CLI, the ee.schimke.composeai.preview Gradle plugin, preview-annotations and the reusable CI composite actions as one release, and this repo pins BOTH halves: the composeai-preview catalog key and the versioned action refs in the compose-preview workflows and design-artifacts.yml. Group them into one PR and skip the batching window so the CLI and the action code that drives it never skew. Only compose-ai-tools' own artifacts: Livery and rc-players also publish under ee.schimke.composeai but are separate projects with their own releases and rules below.

Livery is versioned through its BOM (livery-bom), which pins every Livery module, livery-publish and the Gradle plugin's jar included; the catalog declares the modules without versions. The `livery` version ref also pins the ee.schimke.composeai.livery.catalog plugin, which a BOM can't cover, so group the BOM and the plugin marker into one PR.

The Remote Compose players (rc-player-*, the vendored AndroidX creation fork) are versioned only through rc-players-bom; the catalog declares the modules without versions, so the BOM is the one update.

Every com.squareup.okhttp3 artifact is published from one release and only supports being used at a matching version — okhttp, okhttp-coroutines and logging-interceptor all sit on the same classpath in backend/service-import. Renovate's monorepo data does not group them from Maven metadata alone, so v5.5.0 arrived as three independent PRs, each of which skews the classpath until the last one merges. The catalog now shares one `okhttp` version ref, which groups the declared entries; this rule keeps the guarantee for any okhttp3 artifact declared outside the catalog.

kotlinx-datetime publishes a parallel `-0.6.x-compat` line for consumers still on the pre-kotlin.time.Instant API — which is what apollo-adapters-kotlinx-datetime needs. Plain 0.8.0 sorts ABOVE 0.8.0-0.6.x-compat in Maven ordering, so without this Renovate offers what looks like a routine patch bump and silently moves the repo off the compat line. Restrict updates to the compat line; delete this rule once the datetime consumers are on the new Instant API.

AGP 9.3.x+ outruns what the locally installed Android Studio supports — sync fails with unsupported-AGP-version and "could not find compile target" errors. Hold AGP updates until Studio's bundled support catches up.

Gradle 9.7.x breaks Gradle sync in the current stable IntelliJ IDEA when the Kotlin Multiplatform plugin is enabled, so 9.7.0/9.7.1 were reverted back to 9.6.1. CI is green on 9.7.1 and gives no signal about this — the breakage is IDE-side only — so without this rule Renovate re-offers the bump and it looks safe to merge. Cap the wrapper below 9.7.0, which still allows 9.6.x patches. Lift once IntelliJ ships KMP sync support for 9.7.x.

KEEP IN SYNC WITH settings.gradle.kts. Renovate parses that file statically and cannot follow the loop that declares the repositories, so it detected none, fell back to Maven Central, and reported all 47 Google-Maven-only dependencies as "no-result" — silently freezing androidx out of updates. plugins.gradle.org is here because Renovate skips Maven Central for plugin markers. The apollo-snapshots repo is omitted on purpose: it is filtered to SNAPSHOTs, which Renovate must not offer.

website/ installs with pnpm, whose minimumReleaseAge (1 day) policy rejects any lockfile entry published less than a day ago. Backend Deploy runs that install, but PR CI doesn't, so a Renovate PR for a same-day release (graphiql 6.0.1, 2026-11-07) shows green, merges, and then breaks every deploy until the packages age out. Hold npm updates for the same day so Renovate only proposes versions pnpm will accept. Packages from one monorepo release (graphiql + @graphiql/*) are published together, so this also covers their transitive entries.
